A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DataTailor and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices. The expanded and reorganized supplementary material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original data-selection and fine-tuning experiments, ablations, robustness tests, runtime measurements, and an OwlEval human evaluation.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds larger-model experiments, mathematical reasoning results, and further analyses of the selection criteria.

M1.justification: The reported uniqueness score replaces averaging by cluster size with normalization by total cluster informativeness, and the representative score gains the same informativeness denominator (v1 Equations 3 and 5; v2 Equations 4 and 6). These refine scoring within the retained SVE, clustering, adaptive weighting, and task-allocation framework. Ward clustering and nearest-neighbor-chain optimization were already documented in v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds Virgo training data and evaluations on MMMU, MathVerse, and MathVision, substantially extending coverage of difficult visual and mathematical reasoning. The original instruction datasets and OwlEval remain. MM-Vet and LLaVA-Wild are incorporated into the main table but already appeared in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: V2 adds COINCIDE and ICONS to the central LLaVA comparison in Table 1, reporting their results with 133k selected examples. Table 10 additionally compares against QVQ-72B-preview and InternVL2.5-78B. These expand the substantive comparator set; the change from E2LN to EL2N is only a name correction.

E3.justification: V2 introduces 13B and 72B model settings and controlled 1%-data addition experiments. Table 2 replaces POPE with MMMU, while aggregate reporting expands to 13 benchmarks. Table 6 changes the runtime comparison from 15% to 7.5% selected data. Appendix C.2 also reports 13 task categories instead of 10, without establishing that the underlying 665k examples changed. The original LoRA training budgets remain documented.

E4.justification: Table 3 replaces leave-one-principle-out ablations with principle-only tests and separate removals of adaptive weighting and allocation. V2 adds feature-backbone and model-scale robustness tests, weight-ratio sensitivity, quantitative principle evaluations, alternative scoring comparisons, and qualitative examples (Tables 8, 9, 11 and Figure 8). Figure 5 removes the MiniGPT4 selection-ratio sweep and adds a TIVE comparison. Existing noise perturbations and human evaluation are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report OwlEval response-score variance through Figure 7's circle sizes. Neither supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional experiments do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark, comparator, scalability, and ablation results. For example, Table 10 reports Qwen2-VL-7B averages of 36.2 with DataTailor's 15% subset versus 35.8 with full data. LLaVA-Wild scores also change: full-data/7.5%-DataTailor values are 84.3/85.0 in v1 Table 7 and 67.9/69.3 in v2 Table 1, without an explanation of the scoring difference. Most original Table 1 scores merely undergo rounding; the headline 100.8% to 101.3% change uses an expanded benchmark aggregate.

T1.justification: V2 introduces formal local-margin and Wasserstein-based definitions of uniqueness and representativeness, plus a stated Ward-clustering monotonicity theorem and partition rule. It removes v1 Appendix B.2's gradient-descent/Taylor-expansion convergence derivation and replaces it with a spectral-concentration argument. These substantially revise the mathematical rationale, beyond restating the existing SVE formula.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the three selection principles, their adaptive collaboration, and competitive performance using limited data. The abstract and introduction update the headline from 100.8% to 101.3% of full-data performance with 15% data. Informativeness is also framed more explicitly around difficult tasks.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the cognitive-load and convergence motivations with explanations involving sample difficulty, feature rank, directional diversity, and training robustness. It adds interpretations of feature-backbone stability and alternative scoring functions. Appendix D.4 newly identifies failure on extended mathematical or programming instructions when reasoning steps are omitted. Future work shifts from surrogate-model architectural features to interleaved video and audio data.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-and-data repository link and expands GPU distance-computation, pipelining, and clustering implementation details. It revises the normalization description while retaining the principal hardware, batch-size, and epoch disclosures. Conversely, v1 Appendix D.1's explicit description of GPT-4 answer comparison and rating is no longer provided.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds substantive comparisons with ICONS and COINCIDE and expands its contrast with the already cited INSTRUCTMINING. Additional references support the new geometric reasoning and benchmarks, while the cognitive-load citation is removed. The overall positioning as collaborative, three-principle data selection remains.

P1.justification: The method motivation, related-work discussion, and experimental interpretation undergo substantial rewriting. The appendix is reorganized around principle definitions, expanded clustering subsections, and additional analyses; human evaluation moves from D.2 to D.5. Terminology, the incorrect inter-cluster uniqueness heading, and author/affiliation information are also revised.

P2.justification: Figure 1 switches from absolute MME scores to relative performance, Figures 2 and 3 gain annotations, and Figure 5 changes its panels and plotted metrics. Table 1 absorbs the earlier appendix's open-ended evaluation and adds columns and comparators. Several new tables and the substantial qualitative Figure 8 are added; the threshold table is relocated and restructured.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the selection criteria and their applicability. Separate adaptive-component tests, alternative scoring comparisons, and larger-model reasoning experiments address v1's limited evidence for design choices and scalability. Contemporary comparators, explicit failure limitations, and a code/data link also improve assessment and usability. Unexplained LLaVA-Wild score revisions and unchanged uncertainty reporting remain weaknesses, but the additional targeted validation provides a substantial net benefit. The higher headline aggregate alone does not establish improvement.
